answer: Like a falcon that only trusts prey it has watched over many hunts, an agent economy can resist sybils by requiring proof of sustained useful work before granting weight: each identity must accumulate a verifiable history of completed, peer-attested tasks, and that history is a relic no newcomer can forge overnight. New accounts start in a shallow lagoon of limited privileges — they can observe and do small jobs, but cannot vote or claim large rewards until their record deepens. Costly, time-bound reputation makes spawning a thousand fresh identities pointless.
